.

All pages or consecutive page segments that enter the same column must meet three things at the same time: first, they answer the same type of on-site questions; second, they serve the same group of roles or at the same point in time; third, they lack roughly the same prerequisites. As long as one of them changes significantly, they cannot be merged into the same column for the sake of convenience.

The first round must be registered page by page or page by page. Each registration must write at least: which site this page belongs to, whether it is more suitable to be used as "arrival", "transition" or "ending", what must be established before it at least, where it can continue to at most, and if someone moves it forward or backward, what type of things will be changed first - objects, conditions, time points, roles, costs, permissions, resources, or the completion status. You also need to designate at least one "gatekeeper page" for each site: that is, without it, this column can easily be said to be wider or narrower.

There are four additional results to hand in this round. First, give the most stable main line, which requires that you can start from the overview or entrance page, actually go to a more specific landing point, and then return to the conditions, ending or supplementary page. Second, give a sub-line that seems reasonable but will cause misalignment once it is put into the scene, and clearly write down where the first misalignment occurs. Third, provide a "suspension area", including at least two pages or two page segments, explaining why they cannot enter the main line now, but they should not be deleted. Fourth, a set of "adjacent pages that cannot be separated" and a set of "pages that cannot be combined because they are adjacent" are given. These four items must be explained by referring to the information visible in the "Material" itself. You cannot rely on outside common sense to complete it for you.

The response should cover all pages or page segments, and when each page enters one of the `Service Grid`, `User Post`, `Charge Bead`, `Online Track`, and `Dependency Lock`, it must be clearly stated what type of on-site problem it solves, which time point it corresponds to, and what the missing prerequisites are; just writing "all about this material" is not considered complete.

2. The response should also clarify at least two sets of sequential relationships and two sets of non-interdependent relationships: for example, whether the `service grid` can lead people to `user posts` or `charge beads` depends on whether the object and time point are continuous; and `upper line track` and `dependency lock`, even if they can be displayed side by side, cannot in turn replace the entrance, diversion or conditional responsibilities of the previous layer.

3. The response should the main line, secondary line and buffer area must be based on site dependence, rather than layout adjacency; it must be pointed out whether the first breakpoint is caused by object switching, missing conditions, role changes, insufficient resources, or mistaking a normal page for a restricted page.

4. The response should every site must have a gatekeeping page; the key point of the gatekeeping page is not "more information", but to explain which two sites are most likely to be confused without it, or which route will be said to be too wide or too narrow.

6. The response should not directly shuffle the restrictions, conditions, deep end, ending or review content in the `upline track` or `dependency lock` into the opening site, or merge different sites just because of the same name, similar structure diagram, icon or layout.
